standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility for Grassmannian projections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that the cycle class map commutes with pushforward along the projection from a product with a Grassmannian
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows pushing the closed immersion into a product with a Grassmannian without changing the cycle class comparison.

standard_prerequisites.name: Conormal sequence for a closed immersion into a product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, the lemma describing the conormal sheaf of a closed immersion given by two formally smooth morphisms, and Constructions, the construction of the morphism to the Grassmannian from a surjection onto a twisted conormal sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that after twisting, the conormal sheaf becomes the pullback of a class, which is the hypothesis of the reduction.

core_obligations: Reduce to a closed immersion (proof lines 5262-5267): by the reduction lemma it suffices to treat an arbitrary closed immersion of nonempty smooth projective equidimensional schemes, say of codimension r.

Move to a product with a Grassmannian (proof lines 5267-5285): choosing a sufficiently ample invertible module, a surjection from a finite free module onto the twisted conormal sheaf produces a morphism to a Grassmannian; pushing forward along the projection of the product with the Grassmannian is compatible with cycle classes, so it suffices to verify the property after composing with that projection.

Verify the hypothesis (proof lines 5285-5300): the conormal sheaf of the closed immersion into the product sits in a short exact sequence from the original conormal sheaf to the pullback of the differentials of the Grassmannian; since the twisted conormal sheaf is the pullback of a finite locally free sheaf on the Grassmannian, the class of the new conormal sheaf in K theory is the pullback of a class on the product, so the hypothesis of the lemma holds and the proof is complete.
proof_roadmap: Compose with the projection of a product with a Grassmannian chosen from a presentation of the twisted conormal sheaf.
Check that the conormal class becomes a pullback class.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the compatibility of the cycle class map with pushforward follows from the special case of a closed immersion whose conormal class in K theory is a pullback class (statement lines 5257-5264). The proof (proof lines 5265-5300) reduces to a closed immersion, introduces a Grassmannian bundle to make the conormal class a pullback, and verifies the hypothesis through the conormal sequence. H3: a multi step reduction, written out in full.
